title: A Novel Microencapsulated Bovine Recombinant Interferon Tau Formulation for Luteolysis Modulation in Cattle
content: Early embryonic loss is a significant cause of reproductive inefficiency and economic loss in cattle, largely due to inadequate maternal recognition of pregnancy and premature luteolysis. Interferon tau (IFN-τ), a trophoblast-derived signaling molecule, is essential for maintaining corpus luteum function and embryo survival in ruminants, but its rapid degradation and short half-life have limited its practical use. This study developed a novel delivery system for bovine recombinant IFN-τ (brIFN-τ) produced in Pichia pastoris, utilizing chitosan-based microencapsulation and starch-chitosan hydrogels for sustained intrauterine release. The recombinant protein was successfully expressed, purified, and structurally validated, confirming its interaction with bovine interferon receptors. Encapsulated IFN-τ showed controlled, prolonged in vitro release and retained biological activity, demonstrated by increased viability and antiviral response in bovine cells exposed to Mengo virus. In vivo, the microencapsulated formulation was safe and effectively inhibited luteolysis, as shown by sustained progesterone levels and reduced corpus luteum regression compared to controls. These results indicate that hydrogel-delivered, microencapsulated brIFN-τ is a promising biotechnological strategy to modulate luteolysis, enhance maternal recognition of pregnancy, and reduce early embryonic loss in cattle, potentially improving reproductive efficiency and supporting more sustainable livestock management.
